meaning: Carcharhinus, from Greek karcharias “a kind of shark” (from karcharos “saw-like, jagged”, for its teeth) + rhinus, an ancient word for sharks; leucas, from Greek leukos “white”, for its body colour, usually grayish with a white underside
description: A stocky grey shark with a short, blunt snout, small eyes and a tall first dorsal fin. It tolerates fresh water and swims far up rivers, from the Amazon to the Mississippi. It eats mostly bony fish and other sharks, and also rays and turtles.
depth: Usually under 30 m, down to about 150 m
eats: Bony fish, sharks, rays and sea turtles
